findings.description: In `createSaveAll`’s `tap()` download branch, the `Saved ${ready.length}` toast appears before any downloads start, and the count does not change when a download throws. Because the catch only logs the error and leaves the failed photo out of `handed`, a batch with failed downloads reports the full count without telling the user which photos remain available to retry.
findings.title: Save all reports photos as saved before downloads run

citations.citation: Record completion only after the work succeeds

evidence.explanation: The success toast uses `ready.length` and runs before the download loop, while a thrown `download()` call is caught and logged without changing the toast or adding that photo to `handed`. The test `a photo is marked handed over only when its download starts` covers a failure in a three-photo batch but uses a no-op toast, so it does not check the reported count; the two-browser test expects `Saved 5` before checking file contents.

findings.description: `downloadFile()` treats an anchor click as a completed handoff, so `tap()` adds its PID to `handed` even when the browser blocks an automatic download without throwing. When multiple-download permission is denied, later files in a batch can be blocked while Save all says they were saved, and another tap excludes them as already handed over.
findings.title: Blocked downloads vanish from Save all

citations.citation: Chrome can prompt for or block a site's automatic multiple-file downloads through its site permission.

evidence.explanation: The helper only calls `a.click()`; the batch records each PID immediately afterward and filters recorded PIDs out on later taps. Chrome exposes a permission that can prevent a site from automatically downloading multiple files.

findings.description: `tap()` clears `busy` only in `finally` after `await share(list)` settles, with no path to recover if that browser promise remains pending. In that case every later Save all tap returns “Still saving,” so the person cannot reach either a retry or the download fallback without reloading the tab.
findings.title: A stalled share blocks every later batch

evidence.explanation: The browser promise is passed directly into `share`; `busy` remains true throughout the await and is the first condition checked on every subsequent tap.

findings.description: Figma's Save button label is 'Save all 12', which shows the number of received photos. The code hardcodes 'Save all' and never updates it with a count.
findings.title: Button label drops the photo count

evidence.explanation: The design label includes the count. The code label is static.

findings.description: `tap()` keeps a fixed `ready` list across download gaps without rechecking whether `save(p)` has handed over an item. If someone taps an individual photo during that gap, its download starts and is marked handed over, but the batch downloads the same photo again.
findings.title: Photos can download twice during Save all

evidence.explanation: The per-photo path updates the same handed set independently, while Save all snapshots its batch before waiting and does not inspect that set again inside the loop.
